belief: I can never get out of this.
origins: When bills pile up, interest grows, or one setback follows another, the situation can feel like quicksand. Long stress narrows thinking, and past efforts that failed may make a new plan seem pointless. Some people also grew up around families who always owed, which can make debt seem like a permanent condition.
teaches: Scripture does not hide how heavy troubles can be. David says he waited patiently for the Lord, who lifted him up from the pit of despair and set his feet upon a rock. Lamentations says the Lord’s mercies are new every morning. Paul says we are hard pressed but not crushed, perplexed but not in despair. Proverbs says the plans of the diligent lead to profit. These verses do not promise a quick fix. They say that God lifts, that mornings come, and that steady steps matter.
self_statements: Nothing I do will ever make a difference.
I will be paying this off forever.
This is just my life now.
It is too late to fix it.
errors: Predicting that nothing will ever change.
Believing that if I cannot pay it all off, there is no point.
Seeing the whole mountain instead of the next step.
Feeling stuck and concluding that I am stuck for good.
questions: What exactly do I owe, and have I written the numbers down?
What progress have I made, even if small?
What is one thing that has improved in the past year?
Who has gotten out of a hard situation, and how?
What options have I not yet explored, such as counseling, restructuring, or support?
What is the next smallest step?
truth: This season is heavy, but “never” is a prediction, not a fact. God lifts people out of pits, and His mercies are new every morning. I can take one clear step at a time and ask for help along the way.
hw_truths: “Never” is a feeling, not a fact.
God’s mercies are new every morning.
I can ask for help to find options.
I have survived hard seasons before.
God has plans for my good and my hope.
log: Each week, write the amount you owe and one step you took, however small. Watch the page fill up.
actions: List every debt, balance, and minimum payment. Facing the numbers lowers the fear.
Pick one thing, such as a call, a budget, or a conversation, and do it this week.
Contact a nonprofit credit counseling agency or a trusted advisor about options.
Put a visible check on the calendar for every step taken.
prayer: Lord, You lift people out of pits. When I feel stuck, remind me that Your mercies are new each morning. Show me the next step and give me hope that this will not last forever. Amen.
hw_questions: What one step can I take this week?
Who can help me look at options?
What has God done for me in hard times before?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God’s mercies are new every morning, so I can take one step today.”
